summary:
I folded the four track designs into six sequenced plan documents. Decisions I made on your behalf, and the ones I need you to confirm:

DECIDED — Multi-role wins. `UserRole` keeps `userID @unique` but `role String` becomes `roles String[]`, with the old `role` retained as a nullable dual-written mirror for a rollback window. Same for `FacilityAccess.requiredRole` → `requiredRoles String[]`, which is mandatory: a single string cannot express "jcrc OR cca_head may book this room".

DECIDED — I killed two things every track got wrong. (1) No required non-list scalar (`updatedAt DateTime`) may be added to the already-populated UserRole/FacilityAccess collections — Prisma 6 throws on reading a document missing one, and that read now sits in the session callback, which would have hard-broken login for your 11 seeded JCRC users. They are nullable. (2) The `getUserRole` compatibility shim is deleted, not shipped: `roles[0]` is insertion-order-dependent and would silently strip admin powers at facilitiesBooking.ts:131 and :384 for exactly the admin+jcrc user this design exists to support. All three call sites are converted in the same commit.

DECIDED — Data backfill runs BEFORE `prisma db push` and before any code deploy, via `$runCommandRaw`. The "order-independent" claim in one track was unsafe.

DECIDED — Roles are read live in the session callback (never in the JWT — that would give a revoked admin up to 30 days of access), and every authoritative mutation re-reads from the DB rather than trusting the session copy.

DECIDED — Privilege escalation is closed by four guards, not one: a target guard (non-admin cannot touch a user holding admin), a delta guard (both added AND removed roles must be in your assignable set, so a `set` payload cannot strip admin), a transactional last-admin guard, and no self-assignment of a role you lack. Denied attempts are audited.

DECIDED — `requiredRoles: []` now means open-to-all, identical to no row. The "empty means admin-only" semantic was a live footgun.

DECIDED — Telegram-handle uniqueness is dropped from v1: it is a privacy oracle and would lock legacy duplicate holders out of all profile editing.

CONFIRM D-1: Requirement 6 as written is already satisfied — every room except SCRC is open to everyone, so `cca_head` currently confers nothing. Do you want specific rooms gated to `["jcrc","cca_head"]`, or is `cca_head` just forward-looking vocabulary for now? I will not pretend a requirement shipped when it did not.

CONFIRM D-2: Requirement 4 says the dashboard is admin-only, but requirement 5 gives JCRC role-assignment powers, which needs the same screen. I put both on `/admin` with admin-only sub-sections. Confirm, or I split it.

CONFIRM D-3: Should a JCRC member be able to grant `jcrc` to peers (self-replicating), or only `cca_head`? Your wording allows the former; I implemented it, but blocked jcrc-on-jcrc *revocation* so one member cannot wipe the roster.

CONFIRM D-4: Is `E1633673` definitely your canonical E-format userID? ~515 users carry an A-format matric in `User.userID`; a mis-keyed grant silently does nothing. Step 1 of doc 01 verifies this before anything else.

CONFIRM D-5 (blocking doc 04): I need the live Mongo `$jsonSchema` for `User` before writing nulls to `block`/`telegramHandle`. The command is step 0 of that document.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Book an ungated facility | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Book SCRC Room (`requiredRoles: ["jcrc"]`) | yes (implicit bypass) | yes | no* | no |
| See all bookings (`seeAll`) | yes | no | no | no |
| Delete another user's booking | yes | no | no | no |
| Reach `/admin` | yes | yes | no | no |

| Grant `jcrc` | yes | yes (D-3) | no | no |
| Revoke `jcrc` from another user | yes | no | no | no |
| Revoke own `jcrc` (step down) | yes | yes | n/a | n/a |
| Grant/revoke `admin` | yes | **no** | no | no |
| Modify any role of a user who holds `admin` | yes | **no** | no | no |
| Revoke the last remaining `admin` | **no** | no | no | no |

\* pending decision D-1.
decisionsNeeded: D-1 (blocks 01 seed script): Requirement 6 says CCA heads may book rooms, but every facility except SCRC Room already has no FacilityAccess row and is therefore open to everyone. As specified, `cca_head` grants zero capability. Do you want (a) SCRC opened to cca_head as well (`requiredRoles: ["jcrc","cca_head"]`), (b) specific other rooms gated to `["jcrc","cca_head"]` so cca_head becomes meaningful — name them, or (c) cca_head shipped as forward-looking vocabulary only, with the honest note that it confers nothing today? Plan defaults to (c).

D-2 (blocks 03): Requirement 4 says the admin dashboard is a page "nobody else can see", but requirement 5 gives JCRC role-assignment powers, which needs the same user-management screen. Plan puts both on /admin with admin-only sub-segments (audit log, facility access) behind their own guards, and labels the nav link "Roles" for jcrc viewers. Confirm, or split into /admin (admin-only) and /roles (admin+jcrc).

D-3 (blocks 02 guard table): May a jcrc grant `jcrc` to another user, making the role self-replicating without an admin in the loop? Your wording ("can assign roles to users EXCEPT the admin role") allows it and the plan implements it — but blocks jcrc-on-jcrc REVOCATION so a single member cannot wipe the roster. Confirm, or restrict jcrc to granting `cca_head` only.

D-4 (blocks 01 step 3): Is `E1633673` definitely the canonical E-format userID derived from your login email (email.toUpperCase().replace('@U.NUS.EDU','')), and is your account on an @u.nus.edu address? If not, the admin grant writes a row no session will ever match and silently does nothing. Doc 01 step 1 verifies this before any write.

D-5 (blocks 04): I need the live MongoDB $jsonSchema validator for the `User` collection before deciding whether `block`/`telegramHandle` can be set to null. Run the command in 04 step 0 and paste the output. If null is not permitted, clearing a field must use Prisma `unset` instead.

D-6 (affects 01 step 9, low urgency): Keep the legacy `role` / `requiredRole` fields indefinitely as a permanent rollback affordance, or drop them in phase 3? Cost of keeping is ~20 bytes/doc and one dual-write. Plan recommends keeping them until you have run at least one full term on the new shape.

D-7 (affects 02): Should sign-in be restricted to @u.nus.edu? GoogleProvider is registered with no signIn callback, so any Google account can currently mint a session and therefore a canonical userID. Not required by this work, but it is the foundation the admin role sits on.

D-8 (affects 03): When the JCRC roster arrives, what format will it be in — E-format NUSNET ids, A-format matric numbers, or names? Anything other than E-format needs a resolution step through User.email that is not scoped here.
